title: Bash(find:*) Security Tightening — find -exec/-delete No Longer Auto-Approved
description: Security hardening in v2.1.113: `Bash(find:*)` allow rules no longer auto-approve `find -exec` and `find -delete` subcommands. Previously, a wildcard allow rule for `find` would implicitly approve dangerous subcommands that execute arbitrary commands or delete files — a significant privilege escalation vector. Now, `find -exec` and `find -delete` require explicit separate approval even when the base `find` command is allowed. This is a behavioral change that affects existing permission configs. Additionally, running `cd <current-directory> && git ...` no longer triggers a permission prompt when the `cd` is a no-op (quality-of-life fix). Relevant to security-hardened agent configs and heartbeat sessions with broad Bash allow rules.
redundancy_check: NOVEL — registry documents CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB and PID namespace isolation as subprocess security layers, but this is a new behavior change in the Bash permission approval logic itself. No overlap.
action_required: Audit existing Bash(find:*) allow rules in ~/.claude/settings.json — may need to add explicit find -exec rules if agents legitimately use that pattern

evaluation.reasoning: Security hardening awareness with immediate action item. Integration complexity (90): one-time settings audit + registry update — no code changes, no external installs. Audit result: no Bash(find:*) allow rules found in ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/claudeworkspace/.claude/settings.json, or project settings. Zero remediation needed. Capability expansion (50): not new capability, but important behavioral knowledge — prevents silent privilege escalation via existing wildcard allow rules.
